name: Chlorophyll tablets
lead: Chlorophyll tablets contain chlorophyll or, more often, chlorophyllin, a water-soluble semi-synthetic salt of chlorophyll used as a food colouring (E140 and E141).[1] They are marketed as internal deodorants for breath, body, urine and faecal odour.[1]

Wikipedia calls these deodorant claims unsubstantiated.[1] A randomised, double-blind crossover study in 28 colostomy patients found no difference from placebo in subjective odour.[2] Research on chlorophyllin now focuses on radiation-related conditions in registered trials.[3][4][5][6]

paras: Wikipedia credits F. Howard Westcott's 1940s work with identifying chlorophyllin as an odour blocker. Companies added it to toothpaste, soaps and sanitary products around 1950 to 1953, then dropped it as the hype faded; social-media influencers revived it as chlorophyll water in the 2020s.[1] A 1952 paper examined chlorophyll tablets for faecal odours.[7]

A 1989 randomised double-blind crossover study gave 75 mg chlorophyll tablets three times daily to 28 colostomy patients and found their subjective odour assessments did not differ from placebo.[2] A 1952 report reviewed chlorophyll tablets for faecal odour.[7] Separately, registered trials are testing chlorophyllin for radiation-induced urinary bleeding, oral mucositis, gastrointestinal bleeding and rectal cancer treatment; these do not concern appearance or odour.[3][4][5][6]
Laboratory work shows chlorophyllin binds certain mutagens, and animal and cell studies report other biological effects; Wikipedia describes these as early-stage findings.[1]
Tablets are discussed as an internal fix for breath and body odour.

timeline.event: Westcott's research popularises chlorophyllin as an odour blocker.[1]
Paper on chlorophyll tablets for faecal odour published.[7]
Crossover trial in colostomy patients finds no difference from placebo.[2]

lore.intro: Chlorophyll is promoted as an inside-out deodorant.

claims.claim: Chlorophyll tablets reduce body and breath odour
claims.believers: Users and marketers say it neutralises odour from within.
claims.experts: A randomised trial in colostomy patients found no difference from placebo in subjective odour, and Wikipedia describes the claims as unsubstantiated.[2][1]

card.summary: Chlorophyllin pills sold as internal deodorants; the one controlled odour trial found no difference from placebo.

quick.overview:
Chlorophyll tablets are supplements sold to reduce breath and body odour from the inside.

A small controlled trial in colostomy patients found no difference from placebo, and the odour claims are described as unsubstantiated.
quick.mechanism: Chlorophyllin is claimed to bind odour compounds; this is not established for appearance use.
quick.risks: The sources reviewed give no adverse-effect profile. It is a permitted food colouring.
